text: Tyre pressure is the amount of air inside each tyre. It matters because soft tyres wear out fast and use more fuel. Most cars have a number on a sticker inside the door, and drivers check it before a long run. People change the pressure when the load changes: a full car with bags and kids needs a little more air. When they ask an assistant, they might say 'remind me to check my tyres on Saturday' or 'tell me the right pressure for the back wheels'. If your back is sore from bending down, you can ask your phone to swap the reminder to the weekend. Some cars also show a warning light when one tyre is low.

Marco was a cook, and his hands were full of flour when he spoke to the speaker in his kitchen. 'Tell the robot mower to start tomorrow at seven, and keep going every Saturday.' The assistant understood two things: a first start tomorrow at seven in the morning, and a weekly mowing day. It set the mower's schedule for Saturday at seven and said so out loud. Marco then asked if the battery was full. The assistant checked and said the battery was at eighty percent, enough for one long cut. Marco nodded, wiped his hands, and went back to his dough. He wanted to practice a new bread recipe before the weekend, and now the lawn would take care of itself.

A match score is a simple thing: it tells you who is ahead. Fans use it to follow a team without sitting in front of the screen all day. Most people change what they get. They ask for scores only for their own team, or for an alert when a goal is scored. They say things like 'tell me when United scores', 'what's the score now', or 'stop the alerts'. A low score does not always mean a boring game. Many fans also share the result with friends, so they ask the phone to send the final score to the group chat. Every item in the alert list can be turned on or off. Training works the same way: a coach may ask for a reminder an hour before practice.

A sprinkler waters the lawn so the grass stays green. Most sprinklers have a timer that says when to start and how long to run. People change the timer when the weather changes: less water after rain, a little more in a hot week. When they talk to an assistant, they say things like 'water the lawn at six in the morning', 'run the sprinklers for ten minutes', or 'skip today, it rained'. A dog that likes to dig can leave holes in the grass, so some people turn the sprinkler away from that corner. Even a little water at the right time helps more than a lot at noon, when the sun dries it up fast.

A ventilation fan, or just an open window, brings fresh air into a room. It is for clearing out smells, steam and stale air. People change how strong it is: low when they are sleeping, high when they are cooking. They also change when it runs. They might say 'turn the fan up', 'run it for an hour after dinner', or 'make it quieter'. A narrow window lets in less air, so the fan has to work harder. A plant on the shelf can make a room feel fresher, but it does not replace airflow. After a trip to the market with fish or spices in the bag, many people open the kitchen window for a while.

Dana was a busy parent, and she was putting shoes on a toddler when she spoke to her phone. 'Book a haircut for Leo on Friday and remind me an hour before.' The assistant understood two requests in one sentence: a booking and a reminder. It looked at the barber shop near the front of the school and found a free time at a quarter past four. It booked that time and set the reminder for a quarter past three. Then it asked if Dana wanted to save the shop's phone number. She said yes, and the assistant saved it to her contacts. Dana smiled, picked up the toddler, and walked out the door.

When you buy something online, the shop sends you a tracking number. This number is for following the package from the warehouse to your door. People check it when they think the parcel is late. They also change things: a new delivery day, a different address, or a safe place like the back porch. A narrow delivery window, like one hour, is hard to plan around, so many people ask for a wider one. Words they use are 'where is my package', 'deliver it on Monday', or 'send it to my office instead'. If an item is wrong, like a suitcase with a broken zip, they ask for a refund and a pickup.

A motion sensor wakes up a camera or sounds an alarm when something moves near your home. It is for keeping the house safe when nobody is there. People change when it is on: armed when they leave, off when they come back. In the dark, the camera switches to night mode so you can still see the yard. Many people forget to turn the alarm on, so they ask for a reminder or a schedule. They say 'arm the house', 'I'm home, turn it off', or 'tell me if the garage door opens'. The sound of a car engine passing by can trip an old sensor, so some people make it less sensitive.

When you travel, prices in a shop may be in a different currency. The exchange rate says how much of your money one unit of theirs is worth. It is for knowing if something is cheap or fair. The rate changes every day, so people check it before they pay. They also pick a location to compare, like a trip to Japan next month. Words people use are 'how much is that in my money', 'what's the rate today', or 'is it better to wait'. On a humid day at a market stall, you might flash your phone at the seller to show the price you worked out. A small shift in the rate can change the price of a big purchase.

name: mark_leftovers

people say:

- what has been in there the longest
- tell me when the soup is too old
- mark the single slice of pizza as mine

Ines was a cook, and she had ten minutes for a nap before the dinner rush. First she picked up her phone and typed in a hurry: 'find a wierd gift for my brother, he likes birds, under thirty dollars'. The assistant understood that she wanted gift ideas about birds that cost less than thirty dollars. It ignored the typo and showed three ideas. One was a weird teapot shaped like a parrot. Ines laughed and said she liked it. Then she typed, 'book it for delivery by friday'. The assistant ordered the teapot and set the delivery for Friday. Ines closed her eyes and fell asleep for her short nap.

A lost pet notice helps neighbours find an animal fast. Someone posts a photo and says where the pet was last seen. Neighbours then keep an eye out near the cafe, the park or the bus stop. People change the notice often: a new photo, a bigger area, a reward. Words they use are 'make the search wider', 'increase the distance to two miles', or 'post it again'. A sharp photo of the animal's face works better than a blurry one. Noise works in a similar way. If a party is loud, a neighbour might say 'could you keep it down after ten'. A polite note usually works.

Priya was an office worker, and she was walking across the big field behind her building when her phone beeped. The battery was low. 'Make the screen half as bright and turn off whatever I don't need,' she said. The assistant lowered the brightness to half and switched off background updates. Then Priya asked which app used the most power. The assistant said a map app had used more than all the others. She closed it. The sun was sinking in the west, and she still had to pack her bag for tomorrow's trip. 'Will the phone last until I get home?' she asked. The assistant said yes, about four more hours, which was enough.

Lena had just finished a night shift, and her eyes were half shut. In the car she gave a whisper to her phone: 'Take me home, but not by the highway.' The assistant understood she wanted directions home that skip the highway. It said the back roads would take ten minutes more, and asked if that was fine. Lena said it was. A white van pulled out ahead of her, and the assistant told her to turn left in two hundred metres. Before she drove off, Lena also asked for a reminder to refill the humidifier when she got home. The assistant set the reminder to go off when she reached her street.

Omar was an office worker eating lunch at his desk. He typed in a hurry: 'how much powr did the house use yesterday'. The assistant read powr as power and checked the home energy meter. It said the house used twenty-two units yesterday, which was more than the day before. Omar spilled a little coffee on his sleeve and laughed. The assistant also said the biggest use came at six in the evening, shown as a purple bar in the app. Omar remembered that his brother had parked the van in the garage with the charger plugged in all night. He decided to talk to him.

A notification is a small message from an app that tells you something new happened: a like, a comment, a new follower. It is for helping you know what is going on without opening the app all day. People change how many they get. Some want only messages from close friends. They say 'turn off the likes', 'only tell me about comments', or 'be quiet at night'. Notifications can be annoying at breakfast, when your hands are damp from washing up and your cereal is getting soggy. So many people set quiet hours.

Walter was not good with technology, and the solar panel app on his phone confused him. So he spoke to the speaker in the hall. 'Please measure how much electricity the house uses and tell me tomorrow at seven in the morning.' The assistant understood that Walter wanted a report on his electricity use at seven the next day. It said it would do that and set the report. Then Walter asked why the number never seemed to drop. The assistant said the fridge and his grandson's electric motorcycle charger drew a constant amount of power all night. Walter laughed and asked it to remind him to unplug the charger at bedtime. The assistant did.

Person: Remind me to order more cups.
Assistant: Sure. When should I remind you?
Person: When the shelf is half empty.
Assistant: I can't see your shelf, so I can't tell how full it is. I can remind you at a time, or when you reach the shop. Which one do you want?
Person: Tomorrow at nine then. My brother's plane lands at ten, so I want it done before.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at nine to order more cups.
Person: Great. Now I can chill for a bit.

Watering plants is about giving them enough water without drowning them. Most plants like a drink when the top of the soil feels dry. People change how often they water as the season changes: more in summer, less in winter. A smart sprinkler can warn you when rain is coming, so it skips the next watering. Words people use are 'water the tomatoes every second day', 'skip the next one', or 'change it to evening'. A small change in time can mean a lot, because evening watering loses less water to the sun.

Margaret was not good with technology, and the thermostat on the wall had too many buttons. She sat in her soft chair and spoke to the speaker. 'I don't want the heating on all day, just in the evening when it gets cold.' The assistant understood that she wanted no heat during the day. It made a schedule: heating on from five to ten at night, and off the rest of the time. It set the temperature to twenty degrees and said the radiators would reach it in about forty minutes. Margaret asked how much the bill would drop. The assistant said it could not know exactly, but running the heating five hours instead of fifteen could cut use by a large percent.

Tomi was a child, and it was almost bedtime. The heater hummed in the corner, and the ceiling light was too bright for his eyes. First he said to the lamp, 'Dimmer, please.' The assistant understood that he wanted less light, and it turned the lamp down to thirty percent. Tomi shut his book and put it on the shelf. Then he said, 'Warm colour.' The assistant changed the bulb from white to a soft orange glow. Tomi smiled, pulled up his blanket, and said goodnight. The assistant said goodnight back and kept the light low until he fell asleep.

A filter cleans the air or the water that goes through a machine, like a heater, a fridge or a pipe. It is for keeping the machine healthy. Over time it gets dirty, so people change it every few months. They say 'remind me to change the filter in March', 'book a repair', or 'when did I last do it'. Fold the old paper filter into a bag before you throw it away. If a machine starts making a noise in the middle of the night, or a pipe leaks, it is best to call for a repair soon.

Booking a table means telling a restaurant when you are coming and how many people there are. It is for making sure you have a seat, especially on a weekend when places are full. People change a booking often: a later time, more guests, or fewer. They say 'move it to eight', 'make it for six', or 'cancel our table'. If friends drop out, they ask the restaurant to reduce the group, so the table is smaller. The total on the bill at the end depends on what you ordered, so some people also ask to see the menu before they go.

Hana owned a little shop, and the morning sun was falling on her paintings. She spoke to the assistant behind the counter: 'Could you please close the front blinds about halfway, because the sun is strong and I do not want the paintings to fade?' The assistant understood two things: close the blinds halfway, and the reason was the sun. It closed them to the middle and said so. Hana said thank you. Then she asked it to reserve a table at the cafe for noon, since a man from the factory was coming to see her. The assistant booked the table. Hana went back to opening the last box of frames.

A birthday reminder tells you a day ahead that someone's special day is near. It is for not forgetting. People keep dates in a calendar and sync it with their phone, so the reminder shows up everywhere. They change how early they want to know: a week before for a gift, a day before for a card. They say 'remind me about Dad's birthday', 'tell me a week early', or 'put the party at the park on the calendar'. If your feet are sore from shopping, you can order the gift online and have it sent instead.

Person: Hello. I am having lunch with my son's teacher in an hour, and she speaks Spanish. Could you please help me say something kind, because I would like to build a good start with her?
Assistant: Of course. What would you like to tell her?
Person: Thank you for helping him this year.
Assistant: You can say: Gracias por ayudar a mi hijo este año.
Person: Can you say it slowly? I want it to sound smooth.
Assistant: Sure: grah-see-ahs por ah-yoo-dar ah mee ee-ho es-teh an-yo. Practice it a few times on the way.
Person: Thank you, that helps a lot.

Tariq was a driver, and he was on his way home from a long shift. He spoke to his phone: 'Switch on the kettle and tell me when the oven is hot.' The assistant understood two jobs in one sentence. It started the kettle and began watching the oven. His grandma was coming for dinner, and he wanted to make her favourite cake. The assistant said the kettle was on and the oven would be ready in twelve minutes. Tariq asked it to turn on the fancy coffee machine too, because Grandma loved a good cup after dinner. The assistant said it was done.

Sam woke up with a sudden thought and reached for the phone on the bedside table. 'Could you please tell me when the post office opens today, because I need to send my tax forms before the line gets long?' The assistant understood that Sam wanted the opening hours of the nearest post office. It said the post office opened at nine and closed at five. Outside, the snow was starting to melt, and the road was wet. Sam asked the assistant to remind him at half past eight to leave. The assistant set the reminder and wished him a good morning.

Rosa was a gardener, and she cut her finger on a rose bush. She held it up and said to her phone, 'Cut finger, help.' The assistant understood it was a small cut and told her what to do. Press a clean cloth on it. Rinse it with cool water. Put on a bandage. It also said not to touch the cut with dirty gloves, because that can be dangerous. If the bleeding did not stop in ten minutes, it said, she should call for help. Rosa had planned a jog after work, but the assistant said to rest the hand first. She did as it said, and the bleeding stopped.

Grandpa Leo sat in his armchair and sniffed. The air in the living room felt dusty. It was Tuesday, and the heating had been on all morning. 'Purifier on,' he said to the speaker. The assistant understood and turned on the air purifier in the living room at medium speed. Then it said the filter looked dirty and asked if Leo wanted a reminder to change it. Leo said yes, on Saturday. The assistant set the reminder. Soon the room smelled fresh, and Leo went back to his crossword.

A packing list is a list of what you take on a camping trip: a tent, a sleeping bag, a torch, water and food. It is for making sure nothing gets left behind. People change it with the weather: warm coats for the hills, a rain jacket if rain is coming. They say 'what do I need for two nights', 'put a rain jacket on the list', or 'spell it out, I want every item'. Delicious food matters too, so many lists have a line for snacks. One family even took their kitten along in a carrier, and wrote it on the list.

Nina woke up late, and her head was still foggy. She mumbled to her phone, 'Could you please tell me how to spell engine in French, because I have an important email to send to a mechanic in Lyon, and I expect an answer today?' The assistant understood she wanted the French word for engine and how to spell it. It said the word is moteur and spelled it out slowly: m, o, t, e, u, r. Nina typed it into her email and thanked the assistant. It also offered to check the rest of her sentence, but Nina said she would manage. Then she made coffee.

Kofi woke up and saw that it was still early. He spoke softly to the speaker so he would not wake his kids. 'Could you please dim the lamp and tell me where my package is, because I think the toy I ordered for my son should come today?' The assistant understood two things: turn the light down, and track the order. It dimmed the lamp to a gentle glow. Then it said the package had left the depot at six and was out for delivery, and it should arrive by noon. Kofi thanked it and went to make tea.

Person: Nine. Do I need to bring my toothbrush?
Assistant: I can't say what the dentist wants, but most do not need one. I have booked nine on Thursday for twenty minutes.
Person: Thank you, dear.

Holiday lights are strings of small bulbs that people hang on a tree or a house. They are for making the home feel festive. Many people change when the lights turn on and off. Some use a light sensor that switches them on when it gets dark, so they shine only at night. They say 'turn on the lights at sunset', 'keep them on until ten', or 'boost the brightness'. A timer helps too, because nobody wants to climb a ladder in the cold to pull a plug. Some families have only one switch for the whole house.

Jun had just moved to the city, and his alarm clock was broken. His first day at the new job started early. He held his phone and said, 'Wake me, seven.' The assistant understood he wanted an alarm at seven the next morning. It set the alarm and said it would ring with a gentle sound. Jun asked it to also remind him to iron his shirt tonight. The assistant set a reminder for eight in the evening. Jun put his head on the pillow, felt a little less nervous, and fell asleep.
